title: Battle modes
docText: Scenario mode (Epic tab) and generic mode (Battle tab). PvP and PvC, each up to 5 players.
codeBehaviour: Lobby allows 2–5 total players (humans or 1 human + CPUs). Scenario mode is a setup flag; nothing branches on it.
notes: Scenario mode has no distinct behaviour in the engine.

title: All-era / single-era
docText: All-era games draw locations and GP without era limit; single-era restricts.
codeBehaviour: eraMode 'all' picks 7 locations across eras; 'single' filters to the chosen era. GP deck is never filtered by era in either mode.
notes: Single-era mode still deals GP from every era.

title: Starting hand
docText: 4 Great People, 2 Event cards, 8 Follower cards per player, all in hand.
codeBehaviour: gpHand = 4, eventHand = 2, followerHand = 8.

title: Locations on table
docText: All location cards revealed at start, columns = locations, rows = players.
codeBehaviour: 7 locations (NUM_LOCATIONS) chosen at random from data/locations.json; board rendered as a grid.
notes: Doc does not state the number of locations; code uses 7.

title: Follower deck
docText: Not specified.
codeBehaviour: 3 copies of each of the 32 follower templates = 96 cards, shuffled.
notes: Doc never states follower deck size.

title: Event deck
docText: 8 stats × 3 scenario types (24 scenario cards). Hazards are separate.
codeBehaviour: 24 scenario cards (one per stat × type). 8 hazard types in a separate deck used only for random placement.

title: Hazard at game start
docText: Not specified.
codeBehaviour: One random natural hazard is placed on a random location at game start, lasting 1 round.

title: Winning points
docText: Each completed GP achievement = 1 winning point. Highest total wins.
codeBehaviour: CLAIM_ACHIEVEMENT grants +1 winningPoints when achievementTicks ≥ threshold.

title: 5 points ends the game
docText: Game ends when a player reaches 5 winning points, or only 1 player still has GP cards.
codeBehaviour: checkWinCondition: winningPoints ≥ 5, or exactly one player with GP in hand or on board.
notes: Server match model also uses _WINS_NEEDED = 5 but for a different game (see server-model).

title: A. Deploy a Great Person
docText: Once per turn, place a GP from hand to a location; choose public or private.
codeBehaviour: DEPLOY_GP: once per turn (turnActions.deployedGP), isPublic chosen, card flagged justDeployed.

title: B. Add a Follower
docText: Once per turn, add a follower to a location where you already have a GP.
codeBehaviour: ADD_FOLLOWER: once per turn, requires an allied GP at the location.
notes: Li Qingzhao / Michael Jackson traits that lift this limit are not implemented.

title: C. Move cards
docText: Any number of moves per turn, each card at most once.
codeBehaviour: MOVE_CARD tracked per instance in turnActions.movedCards; justDeployed cards cannot move.

title: D. Start an event
docText: A player may start an event only at a location where they have a Great Person that was not deployed this turn; most events are local.
codeBehaviour: START_EVENT places an event card from hand on a location, once per location per turn, and only if the player has a GP there with justDeployed === false (same presence check as END_SCENARIO). Global competitions use the same gate.
notes: In-game rules panel and selection hint say 'where you have a Great Person that was not deployed this turn'. The CPU AI never starts events, so it is unaffected.

title: E. Retrieve to hand
docText: Retrieve a GP or follower from the board to hand.
codeBehaviour: RETRIEVE_CARD returns GP id to gpHand / follower to followerHand; once per card per turn.

title: F. Claim achievement
docText: Claim that a GP on board completed its achievement → 1 winning point.
codeBehaviour: CLAIM_ACHIEVEMENT requires the card public and ticks ≥ threshold; grants +1 point AND immediately draws a new GP card to hand; ticks reset to 0 and the GP stays on board.
notes: Doc: archiving is a separate, optional step that yields the new GP (§6). Code merges both and never archives.

title: G. Attack
docText: Attack any number of times per turn when both players have cards at the same location during a local event.
codeBehaviour: ATTACK allowed only when location.activeEvent.type === 'local_event'; no per-turn limit.
notes: Attacker's card is not required to be public (doc §7 says it must be).

title: H. End a local event
docText: A GP can end a scenario if it has the matching identity (e.g. Artist ends Art Critique).
codeBehaviour: END_SCENARIO: any non-just-deployed allied GP at the location can end any local event or survival, once per location per turn. Identity is not checked.

title: I. Toggle public/private
docText: Change a card's status; once per card per turn.
codeBehaviour: TOGGLE_VISIBILITY once per card per turn; justDeployed cards cannot toggle.

title: Just-deployed cards cannot act
docText: A GP or Follower that was just put on board cannot do C/D/E/F/I this turn.
codeBehaviour: justDeployed flag blocks move, retrieve, claim, visibility, end-scenario; cleared at END_TURN.
notes: Attack (G) is not blocked for just-deployed cards in either doc or code.

title: Phase order within a turn
docText: Deploy GP → Followers → Retrieve → Relocate → Visibility → Attack → Survival → Event → End scenario → New scenario → Achievement → Archive.
codeBehaviour: Free-form: any action can be taken in any order until END_TURN. Survival/hazard/global resolution happens only when a full round completes.

title: Reveal after attack
docText: After an attack, both players' cards at that location must all be public. Defender's cards auto-join and are revealed.
codeBehaviour: Only the two cards named in the ATTACK action are flipped public. Other allied/enemy cards at the location keep their status.

title: Private cards are hidden
docText: Face-down cards cannot be identified by other players.
codeBehaviour: CompactCard renders the card back for private cards of other players. State still contains the card id (client-side game).
notes: Hot-seat PvP: any player at the screen can inspect state via devtools.

title: Scenario names per stat
docText: politics: Coup/Terrorist Attack/International Conference; strength: Battlefield/Riot/Olympics; culture: Art Critique/Censorship/Roadshow; wealth: Business War/Depression/Auction; technique: Tech Race/Sanctions/World Fair; intelligence: Argument/Puzzle/Expedition; belief: Miracle/Inquisition/Pilgrimage; reputation: Lawsuit/Scandal/Celebration.
codeBehaviour: EVENT_NAMES matches the doc exactly.

title: Totals compared
docText: Compare the total of the stat over all GP and Followers of each player at the location (follower bonus included). Stronger side may attack.
codeBehaviour: computeLocationTotal = Σ GP base stat + implemented trait bonus + location bonus per GP, + follower bonus for followers whose stat matches.
notes: Doc has no notion of location bonus or trait numbers; engine adds both.

title: Winner chooses kill or retrieve
docText: Winner (sometimes the defender) chooses: kill → discard pile; otherwise loser is force-retrieved to hand. Draw → nothing.
codeBehaviour: Attacker chooses kill:boolean before attacking. The flag is applied to whichever side loses, so an attacker who loses is killed by its own choice. Draw → nothing. Only the single targeted card is removed, not the whole losing side.

title: Attacker must be public
docText: To attack, the GP must be public; public allied GP/Followers auto-join; defender's cards all revealed.
codeBehaviour: Not enforced: a private GP can attack. All allied cards (public or private) are summed.

title: Follower bonus
docText: 'Any follower bonus' is added to the GP total.
codeBehaviour: Follower adds its bonus (2) if its stat matches the scenario stat; 3 instead if an allied GP at the location has the follower's identity.
notes: Identity-match bonus (+3) exists only in code.

title: Location bonus
docText: Not in fight.md. location_cards.json carries per-stat bonuses and a trait text per location.
codeBehaviour: Each GP at the location gains the location's bonus for the contested stat in conflicts only (not survival/hazard/global). Location trait texts are never executed.

title: Local survival threshold
docText: Any player at this location whose total for the stat (GP + followers) is below 10 is killed and discarded.
codeBehaviour: Threshold is 5: a player survives when total ≥ 5. Resolved at the start of each new round while the event stays active.
notes: iOS/Android rules dialogs say 10. Card stats range 1–12, so a single GP survives at 5 only with a decent stat.

title: Survival persists
docText: The scenario keeps working until replaced by another event or ended by a GP.
codeBehaviour: eventRoundsLeft = 99 for local events/survival; replaced by START_EVENT or cleared by END_SCENARIO.

title: Special survival (hazard)
docText: Flood/Blizzard/Storm/Earthquake/Fire/Tsunami/Pandemic/Drought. Any player with total points (all stats, GP + followers) below 100 is killed. Random, lasts 1 round, placed where the drawer has most cards.
codeBehaviour: Per player: sum each of the 8 stats across their cards at the location; if the MINIMUM stat total < 5 they are discarded. 20% chance per new round, placed on the location with the most cards. Lasts 1 round. Hazard type has no effect.
notes: iOS/Android rules text says 'total stats below 100'. Three different rules exist.

title: Global competition
docText: All players involved; lasts 1 round; highest total of the stat over all PUBLIC cards on the board wins 2 events, 4 followers or 1 GP.
codeBehaviour: Sums base stat of public GP only (followers, traits and location bonuses ignored). Winner picks reward: 2 events / 4 followers / 1 GP.
notes: Followers excluded in code; doc says all cards.

title: Scenario replacement
docText: A scenario stays until replaced by another event or ended by a GP.
codeBehaviour: START_EVENT overwrites activeEvent at the location.

title: Trait-driven scenario negation
docText: Gandhi negates all Conflict scenarios; Schumann shields from Survival for one round; Mani immune to Survival.
codeBehaviour: No scenario-level trait hooks exist.

title: Archive to draw a new GP
docText: A GP that completed its achievement may be archived (while public); owner then draws a new GP.
codeBehaviour: No ARCHIVE action. PlayerState.archive exists but is never written. New GP is drawn on claim instead.
notes: Turing / Bi Sheng / Gutenberg traits that key off 'last archived GP' cannot work without archiving.

title: Global competition reward
docText: Winner of a global competition gets 2 event cards, 4 follower cards or 1 GP card.
codeBehaviour: GLOBAL_COMP_REWARD draws exactly those amounts from the respective decks.

title: Trait text is per-card data
docText: Each GP has a Characteristic (trait) that works while in the game.
codeBehaviour: traitBonusForGP implements numeric bonuses for 13 figures only; the other 67 traits have no effect. Several implemented bonuses differ from the card text (see Great People tab).

title: Trait idea doc vs cards.json
docText: great-people-trait-idea.md lists 28 draft traits/achievements.
codeBehaviour: cards.json is the shipped text; several entries were rewritten (e.g. Aspasia, Enkidu, Mani, Eisenstein, Peck) and some doc entries are blank (Musashi, Brahms, Titian, Clara, Montezuma, Mendel).
notes: Decide which document is canonical.

title: CPU visibility heuristics
docText: Not specified.
codeBehaviour: CPU keeps Belisarius, Musashi, Mao private and reveals Pericles/Aspasia-style cards; references traits that are not implemented (Musashi, Mao).

title: Achievement conditions
docText: Each GP has a named achievement with a specific in-game condition (see card text).
codeBehaviour: None of the textual conditions are evaluated. Instead: a GP earns 1 'tick' when it attacks and KILLS an enemy GP in a conflict whose stat equals the GP's ACHIEVEMENT_SPECS stat and the victim has ≥ 5 in that stat. Threshold 1 tick for the 47 mapped figures, 3 ticks for the other 33.
notes: Every achievement is effectively 'kill one worthy GP in your stat'. Defensive, positional and cooperative achievements are impossible.

title: Stat scale assumptions
docText: Al-Khwarizmi's achievement needs base stats 1–25; Brahms' trait uses a 25 threshold.
codeBehaviour: cards.json stats range 1–12 (demo_cards.json 1–24). Brahms implemented with a 13 threshold.
notes: Clarify the intended stat scale.

title: iOS/Android rules dialogs
docText: Not applicable (apps show a summary).
codeBehaviour: Both show: Local Survival discards cards below 10; Natural Hazard discards below 100; events triggered where you have a GP. Neither app runs the engine (online match placeholder only).
notes: Mobile text follows fight.md numbers; web engine uses 5 / min-stat 5.

title: Backend battle model
docText: great-people-card.md describes an older 10-card deck, simultaneous-play, 3-stat (Influence/Innovation/Legacy) round game, first to 5 rounds.
codeBehaviour: service/api/battle.py resolves a round by comparing one stat (round.active_stat) of two CardDefinition cards; first to 5. It does not model locations, followers, events or achievements. The web board game is purely client-side.
notes: Two different battle designs are documented; the board game only exists in the web client.
